How to Paste Images, GIFs, and Screen Captures into After Effects

Use Vampro Universal Paste to bring clipboard media, screen recordings, and video links into a composition, then swap footage when your design changes.

Darshan
November 22, 2026 · 5 min read

Overview

Coming Soon: Vampro Universal Paste for Adobe After Effects is releasing soon. Here is a preview of the upcoming workflow.

Say you're building a product demo in After Effects. You need a screenshot for the first shot, an animated reference for a transition, and a temporary product image while the final render is on its way. Each asset normally starts another round of saving, finding, and importing files.

Vampro Universal Paste puts those steps inside one panel. The Windows companion prepares the media, and After Effects imports it into the Project panel or adds it as a layer at the playhead. Later, you can swap the source of an animated layer when the final asset arrives.

Open Universal Paste in After Effects Coming Soon

Start with After Effects 25 through 27 on 64-bit Windows 10 or 11 and Vampro Universal Paste Companion v1.1.0 or newer. If you already use the companion with Premiere Pro, keep using that installation. It serves both apps.

  1. Install the After Effects edition and launch the companion.
  2. Open Window → Extensions → Vampro Universal Paste and check for Companion Connected.
  3. Save your .aep project. Open a composition and place the playhead where you want the new layer to begin.

The companion saves imported media under Assets beside the project. In the After Effects Project panel, look for the matching Assets folder and its media subfolders.

Paste an image or animated GIF

In your browser, use Copy image on a reference you want to use. Switch to the Clipboard tab and check the preview. You can also paste a supported image, GIF, or video URL into the Source field.

For a still image, choose a duration and how it should fit the composition. Fill Frame covers the frame and may crop the edges. Original Size keeps the source scale. Select Paste to Composition to place the layer at the playhead, or Import to Project to save the footage for later.

When Universal Paste receives the animated GIF or a supported GIF URL, the companion converts it to an MP4 so it plays as motion in After Effects. If the browser copies a single still frame, paste the original GIF URL or copy the GIF file. For a still-image cutout, choose Remove Background, preview the transparent PNG, and import or paste it. Use Original switches back to the source image.

Grab a screenshot or record your screen

Open Capture → Screenshot. Choose Entire Display or App Window, then capture the full source or use Snip Region. When the panel prompts you to switch windows, go to the selected window yourself. For a snip, draw the region when the snipping tool appears.

For motion, choose Screen Record. Set your target, select Full Source or Snip Region, and pick With Sound or Muted. Start the recording workflow, switch to the target when prompted, and choose a region if you selected a snip. The recorder shows a three-second countdown and provides pause and stop controls. With Sound uses Windows system audio.

When the capture preview is ready, choose Insert into Composition or Import to Project. Use Clear to reset the panel before starting the next capture.

Bring in a video from a link

Paste a supported link into Video and click Fetch. Review the thumbnail and any available details, such as duration and resolution. Download and Insert adds the video to the active composition. Download to Project imports it as footage. The companion requests the best available supported version with audio. Online sources require an internet connection and depend on what the source site makes available.

Swap footage after you’ve animated it

When the final asset arrives, select an unlocked footage layer in the composition and open Replace. Confirm the target, then choose Clipboard or URL for the new source. Review the preview and choose Replace Layer.

The replacement can go from image to video or video to image. The same layer retains its effects and keyframes. Leave Auto-fit replacement to composition frame unchecked when you want to keep the current scale. If you select a footage item in the Project panel instead, replacing it updates the layers that reference it.

Try it on a rough comp. Paste a still at the playhead, animate it, then replace it with your final media. The layer and its animation are already there, and both source files are easy to find in the project’s asset folders.
